items.title: fix(cli): keep one-shot databases open until admitted detached work s…
items.summary: fix(cli): keep one-shot databases open until admitted detached work settles (#207510) ## Problem A one-shot command (`openclaw agent --local`, `agent exec`, `templates add`) closes its databases as soon as its own turn returns. Work the command admitted that runs detached from the turn (subagent completion, announcements back to the parent, cleanup flows) is cut off: its next database write fails with `Database maintenance resource admission is closed`, and the result is lost without a visible error. ## Solution One owner waits: the one-shot database owners wait for admitted root work to go idle before they close the databases. - `waitForGatewayRootWorkIdle` (process/gateway-work-admission.ts): resolves when no root work outside the caller is active. It is event-driven (root-work release listeners, no timer). Long-lived subscriptions never count, by the existing `isActiveRootWork` rule, so a process that hosts no Gateway cannot wait on listeners or loops. - `waitForLocalBackgroundWork` (cli/local-state-owner.ts) is the single call both one-shot owners use: `runWithLocalStateOwner` before it closes its resources, and `agent exec` before it cleans up its temporary state. - While it waits, the CLI prints `Waiting for N background tasks to finish. Press Ctrl-C to stop.` Ctrl-C stops the wait: through the CLI signal gate, or through the command's own signal bridge for `agent --local` and `agent exec`. ## User impact - One-shot commands that started detached work keep their databases open until it finishes, with one visible waiting line. - Commands that start no detached work exit as before, with no wait. - Gateway users: unchanged. The wait runs only in the one-shot owners. - This is part A of a split. Part B (subagent spawn in one-shot `agent --local`) builds on it. ## Accepted edge cases - **Ctrl-C** stops the wait, not the work. The databases then close under any work still running, which is what main does today for all detached work. - **Failure retries on timers** hold no root work during the delay, so a one-shot process can exit before a retry runs. The work stays persisted as pending; the next Gateway start recovers it. ## Evidence - New test `local-state-owner.test.ts` "keeps the command's databases open until detached work it admitted settles": red on main (the owner settles while the detached work is still held), green here. - `gateway-work-admission.idle.test.ts`: no work or only a subscription returns at once; detached work is waited for and reported once; an interrupt stops the wait. - Consumer tests of every changed module pass. Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi
